newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's economy improves in first half 1997.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's economy improves in first half 1997.

text.p: The Moroccan economy, excluding the agriculture sector, grew an estimated 3.5 percent in the first half of the year compared with the same period in 1996, the finance ministry said.
In its monthly newsletter, the ministry said: "Gross Domestic Product (GDP), rose in real terms 3.5 percent in the first half of the year due to the resumption of the country's economic activity".
But agriculture output, which is expected to drop dramatically due to adverse weather, was not included in this figure, the ministry said.
Morocco's cereals harvest fell to 3.35 million tonnes in the 1996/97 season from 10 million tonnes the previous season, the agriculture ministry said earlier.

The finance ministry said phosphates and derivatives, the country's main mining exports, rose 33.6 percent in value to 6.2 billion dirhams ($620 million) from January to June 1997 compared with 4.6 billion dirhams in the first half last year.
According to the ministry's newsletter, domestic cement sales rose 16.4 percent to confirm the resumption of public works and construction sectors in the first half of the year.
Foreign investments and loans jumped nearly 300 percent to 5.97 billion dirhams compared with 1.49 billion in the first half of 1995, it said.
Food imports fell 25.6 percent to 4.39 billion dirhams in the first half year compared with the first half of 1996.

Inflation fell to 0.2 percent in the first half of the year compared with 3.4 percent in the whole year of 1996, the ministry said. The net change was attributed to a decline in the food index, it said, but gave no comparative figures for the first half of 1996.
Morocco's foreign assets improved by an average 16.6 percent between December 1996 and June 1997.
Remittances by Moroccan expatriates and earnings from tourism fell by by 5.7 percent and 2.9 percent respectively compared with the previous period, the ministry said. ($1= 10 dirhams)
